notes: Counters are judged against red's full six on every board, whatever red had revealed.
With nothing revealed, CounterWatch's builder reads no counters, while Countrix reads red's likely six from Blizzard's pick rates.
With all six revealed, the CounterWatch blend solved exactly is the yardstick's own best six, so exact against slot by slot is read by reveal moment.
CounterWatch's matchup win rates carry each hero's own strength; its duel ratings are centred, the cleaner counter reading. Its duo win rates (synergy) carry strength too.
CounterWatch's pair-minus-heroes 'kit synergy' was dropped: a pair is shrunk harder than a hero, which reads strong sixes below random.

CounterWatch's six is a reconstruction of its documented builder, not the button's output; HeroStats' and OW Hero Stats' sixes are their documented formulas run on Blizzard's rates (HeroStats' log taken as natural), not their sites' output.
Editorial tier lists state no model and refuse automated readers, so they are left out.
Blizzard's rates are 5v5 Role Queue on console; CounterWatch's are 6v6 on PC. Neither yardstick is match results: no 6v6 match outcomes exist to judge against.

The test-half maps are no clean hold-out: the 2026-10-04 halving of Countrix's synergy and counter dials was chosen with their results in view. The fresh red sixes are draws no tuning saw. Train against test is no clean check of generalization.

theorems.name: The six is the best legal six
theorems.statement: No legal six scores higher than the six Countrix returns; ties go to the published tie-break, and a search that cannot prove its answer refuses instead of guessing.
theorems.formal: for every legal y: round(score(y), 9) <= round(score(x*), 9)

checked.method: brute force (prove_exact) of every legal six against the search
no legal six scored on a board outranks its optimum (every arm's six, 1,000 random sixes, the reference sixes legal there)
checked.skipped_why: sixes not legal on their board, left out of the check: the reference sixes that field a banned hero on a ban board (the scale's sample holds still under bans, by design) and any other six that fields a banned hero or breaks a limit

checked.method: searches refused (past the budget or no legal six)

theorems.name: No six beats it on every count
theorems.statement: No legal six does at least as well on the default engine's three terms and on every rule's term, and better on one: a six that gains on the meta gives up synergy, counters or a rule.
theorems.formal: no legal y with T_k(y) >= T_k(x*) for every term k and > for one

checked.method: dominance over every other arm's six and the random and reference sixes legal on the board

theorems.name: The Meta slider trades in one direction
theorems.statement: Turning the Meta slider up never lowers the engine's part of the optimal six and never raises the playbook's.
theorems.formal: mu1 < mu2 => B(x2) >= B(x1) and H(x2) <= H(x1)

checked.method: each slider step's six scored on the meta-1 objective

theorems.name: A rule's weight buys its own satisfaction
theorems.statement: Raising a rule's weight never lowers that rule's own term on the optimal six.

checked.method: each rule at its weight against the same rule at 0

theorems.name: A team, not a list
theorems.statement: The engine is supermodular - a pick is worth more beside its partners - so the best six need not hold the best single picks, and a slot-by-slot fill can miss it.
theorems.formal: measured: exact search against the slot-by-slot fill

theorems.name: No hidden favourite
theorems.statement: With nothing scoring, every legal six ties and a hash of the map, the side and the hero settles it, which seats every hero of a role about equally often.
theorems.formal: null objective: each hero seated within a quarter of its role's mean

data_swap.note: Countrix's engine and playbook, unchanged, solved on a World whose rates are CounterWatch's 6v6 ones (win rate its shrunk 6v6 win rate, pick rate its 6v6 pick rate, map rates its 6v6 map win rates), held in memory

legend.rows: red, bans and each six are indices into heroes; sixes lists one six for each of row_arms[set], in that order; values lists, for each of row_values[set].arms, its row_values[set].metrics in that order; search is [legal sixes, branches walked, sixes scored in full, seconds, sixes tied]; moves and applies are indices into rules: the rules whose removal changes cx_full's six, and the rules whose term applies to it
